recruit_text.backstory: Sherif did pest control in Cairo, fumigating apartment blocks and restaurants and once, memorably, a museum storeroom. He's spent his whole working life very calm around things that sting, and the Royal Hive is full of them. He arrived with his fumigation rig on his back and found out venom listens to him here. He's unbothered, amused and the only person who walks into the hive without flinching.

stages.stranger: I'm Sherif, a venomancer. Don't swat at them, ya basha. Things that sting only get worse when you panic, and they can tell.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Shubra, in Cairo. My father started a pest control business in 1987 with one van, and I joined at twenty-three. Fifteen years of apartment blocks, restaurant kitchens, and once a storeroom at the Egyptian Museum, where beetles were eating a crate with a big label telling you to keep it shut. I didn't open it. I'm still curious.
stages.companion: I was engaged to Mariam, a pharmacist. I met her when I came to fumigate her pharmacy, and she told me exactly which chemicals she didn't want near her stock. She was right about every one. The wedding was set for the spring. I was fogging a restaurant kitchen when everything changed, and this nozzle's the only part of my rig that survived the landing.
stages.friend: This is the part I keep to myself, ya basha. I'm afraid she was in the pharmacy, and the pharmacy didn't cross over. That's why I ask every healer. And now there's a sickness from the hive's stings spreading through the camps, and nobody can treat it. My catalogue says the answer's in a sample from the deep chambers, further in than anyone's been. Will you come down with me?
stages.sworn: Leading the healers who came for the antidote was a woman with a pharmacist's bag, and she looked at my work and told me exactly which part was wrong. She was right. It was Mariam. She's been in the camps for two years, sending notes to every hub asking after a pest controller who'd be near things that sting. I laughed until I couldn't breathe. We fixed the antidote together, and I asked her if the spring wedding was still on. She said it's always spring somewhere. Take the nozzle. I don't need to fog anything any more.

moments.prompt: A huge hive insect lands on your shoulder. Sherif is watching, very calm.

options.reply: That's it, ya basha. See, it's leaving, and nobody had to die.
Maalesh, now it's angry. Next time, stand still.

moments.prompt: He's asked you to go into the deep chambers with him.

options.reply: Yalla, ya basha. Stay behind me, move slowly, and don't swat anything.
Deeper than anyone's come back from. That's why I want company.

lines.bored_warning: Ya basha, there's nothing new out here to catalogue. Take me somewhere with a proper infestation.
lines.leaving_good: Good job, that, clean and tidy. I'll be in the first chambers of the Royal Hive, writing it all up.
lines.leaving_bored: Same bugs, same fields, same everything. The hive's more interesting, so I'm going back there.
lines.after_wipe: Maalesh, everybody, it happens. Get up slowly and don't swat at anything.
lines.wipe_warning: This place is eating us like termites in a doorframe. After this run, I'm going somewhere peaceful, like the hive.
lines.wipe_leave: Khalas, I'm done for now. You'll find me in the Royal Hive, where the stings make sense.
lines.zone_warning: This is an infestation we can't handle, ya basha. Even I'd call for backup on this one.
lines.zone_leave: Some jobs you turn down, and this is one. I'll be in the first chambers of the Royal Hive.
lines.gear_refuse: Not that one, ya basha, sorry. My father taught me never to lend out good kit.
lines.gear_taken: Maalesh, take it, and I'll improvise.
lines.gear_short: Gaps are where pests get in, ya basha, and I've got one in my kit.
lines.gear_upgrade: Ya salam, that's lovely. Thank you.
lines.back: The hive catalogue has thirty new pages. Yalla, where's the job?
lines.send_word: Sherif has sent word from the Royal Hive. His notes are up to date and he's ready.
lines.walkout_talk: That temper wasn't me, ya basha, and I'm sorry. Sit down and I'll tell you what got under my skin.
lines.neglect: Ya basha, you're back! I was about to put your name on my list of rare sightings.
lines.asked_to_stay: Maalesh, one more. The bugs aren't going anywhere.
lines.on_break: Sherif is back in the first chambers of the Royal Hive, cataloguing. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

town_arrive.text: There's a koshari cart at the end of my street in Shubra, and the man knows my order before I open my mouth. I'd fight a hive for a bowl right now.

zone_arrive.text: Look at the size of that beetle. Don't worry, ya basha, it's more scared of you than you are of it.

close_call.text: Calm, calm, it can smell fear. Back away slowly with me.

dungeon_clear.text: I counted four new species in there. Nobody step on anything on the way out.
